items.text: The method: reduce to sets by replacing each object by the functor it represents.
Two constructions: from a quotient to a relation, from a relation to a quotient.
F\twoheadrightarrow G\ \ \leadsto\ \ R=F\times_G F\subset F\times F
Check argumentwise (parameter $Z$): $R$ is an equivalence relation. Any map $F\to G$ will do, not only an epimorphism.
Conversely, from $R\subset F\times F$: the two projections give a double arrow, and the quotient is its cokernel.
A quotient $F\to G$ is effective if it is the quotient of its own relation $F\times_G F$.
A relation $R$ is effective if $R=F\times_{F/R}F$ (a priori $R$ is smaller).
\{\text{equivalence relations on } F\}\ \longleftrightarrow\ \{\text{quotients of } F\}\quad\text{(all effective)}
True in $\mathbf{Sets}$; stated with finite inverse limits and direct limits only.
So it carries over: in $\operatorname{Top}(X)$ every equivalence relation and every quotient is effective.
